360 ONE WAM Earnings Call - Q2 FY27  Mr. Anil Mascarenhas - Sr. EVP, Communications, 360 ONE WAM:
 Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to 360 ONE WAM's earnings call for
Q2 FY27. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only mode. In case you wish to ask a question or require assistance during the call, kindly signal the host by tapping on the raised hand icon. Please note, this conference is being recorded.
 On the call today, we have with us Mr. Karan Bhagat, MD and CEO, Mr. Yatin Shah,
CEO of the Wealth Business, Mr. Anshuman Maheshwary, CEO of 360 ONE Alternates, and Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa, our CFO. I now hand it over to Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa to take this call forward.
 Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa - Chief Financial Officer, 360 ONE WAM Limited:
 Thank you, Anil. A very good evening to all the participants.
 Starting with the macros, Q2 was a quarter of two halves for Indian equities. Benchmark

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ROHIT S. BHASE
chunks.text:
 Starting with the macros, Q2 was a quarter of two halves for Indian equities. Benchmark
indices stayed under pressure through the quarter, weighed down by persistent FPI selling, global rate concerns, and geopolitical uncertainty. At the same time, domestic flows and primary markets were remarkably resilient. Monthly SIP flows touched a record of ₹32,500 crores in September, and close to 70 companies raised ₹90,500 crores through IPOs during the quarter, including the landmark listing of NSE. We continue to believe that the long-term tailwinds clearly outweigh the near-term concerns. Let me call out four of them:
 First, wealth creation in India. The UHNI segment continues to grow at 13 - 15%, and monetization events such as IPOs, block deals, stake sales, keep releasing liquidity to promoters and families.
 Second, the financialization of savings. SIPs, the newly launched SIF category, and democratization of AIFs are steadily expanding the investable pool.
 Third, the shift to professional wealth management. Clients increasingly want transparent, fee-based advice, and a growing number of family offices want curated access to opportunities.
 And fourth, global connectivity. Resident Indians want to invest globally, global institutions are refocusing on India, and Gift City is opening new opportunities in asset management and broking.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ROHIT S. BHASE
chunks.text:
 And fourth, global connectivity. Resident Indians want to invest globally, global institutions are refocusing on India, and Gift City is opening new opportunities in asset management and broking.
 We remain mindful of the near-term challenges, including market volatility, competition,
evolving regulation, and pressure on costs. Our response is to stay the course, give the right advice to our clients, while running the business in our shareholders' interest.
 Now, coming to our performance for the quarter, total AUMs stood at about ₹9 lakh
crores, up 31% year-on-year. ARR AUMs stood at ₹3,53,000 crores, up 19.7% year-on- year, and ARR net flows of ₹12,482 crores during the quarter, compared to ₹10,815 crores in Q1. Clients with more than ₹10 crores of AUM are over ₹4,100 and account for 95% of our ex-custody wealth AUM.
 Revenue from operations was ₹896 crores, up 17.5% year-on-year. ARR revenue grew

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ROHIT S. BHASE
chunks.text:
 Revenue from operations was ₹896 crores, up 17.5% year-on-year. ARR revenue grew
27.5% y-o-y to ₹706 crores. ARR now contributes 79% of operating revenues, and ARR retention improved to 79 basis points from 74 basis points in Q1, driven by higher carry income for the quarter. Excluding carry income, the ARR retentions remained stable at 67 basis points. During Q2, carried interest from third-party funds contributed approximately ₹60 crores. Transaction and brokerage income was ₹190 crores, down 9.1% year-on-year. Other income was negative ₹44 crores this quarter, primarily on account of mark-to-market impact on our treasury investments. As a result, total revenue was ₹853 crores, up 4.8% year-on-year.
 Total costs were ₹462 crores, up 15.5% year-on-year. Employee costs were ₹342
crores, up 19.9%, and include a one-time impact of about ₹9 crores from restructuring of one of our businesses. Admin and other costs were ₹120 crores, up 4.6%. Our cost- to-operating income ratio improved to 51.5% from ₹54.3 in Q1.
 Operating PBT grew 19.7% year-on-year to ₹434 crores. Given the lower other income,
PBT was ₹391 crores and PAT was ₹302 crores, against ₹316 crores in Q2 FY26. Tangible ROE stood at 16.9%. The board approved a second interim dividend of 7.5 per share.
 The wealth business saw a strong quarter, backed by strong flows and higher retentions.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ROHIT S. BHASE
chunks.text:
 The wealth business saw a strong quarter, backed by strong flows and higher retentions.
ARR AUM grew 24.3% year-on-year to ₹2,52,627 crores. 360 ONE Plus, our advisory platform, has now crossed ₹1 lakh crores. The quarter saw net flows of ₹10,990 crores that were broad-based across engagement models. New client additions and deeper wallet share with existing clients contributed towards the flow. ARR revenue grew 40.5% year-on-year to ₹503 crores. Retention improved to 79 basis points from 71 basis points in Q1. Operating PBT grew 30.2% year-on-year to ₹326 crores. The UHNI franchise remains the firm's anchor with unchanged priorities, grow share of wallet, widen our reach beyond the metros, and be the first call for families after a liquidity event. That last point matters more than ever, given record IPO and monetization activity over the last few years. More clients are moving to portfolio-level advisory mandates, which make relationships deeper and stickier. The HNI business continues to scale as a natural extension of UHNI. It now manages over ₹8,000 crores at healthy retentions for over 1,500 clients and about 60 relationship managers. With productivity improving and a growing feeder pipeline into UHNI, we expect the business to break even on direct costs soon. With the business reset behind us, ET money is now built for profitable growth. Its base of 5.5 lakh plus active users is being taken towards a full lifecycle digital wealth platform. Clients will choose upfront between distribution and subscription-based advisory, and AI-assisted advice will extend into affluent segments. The distribution segment of the business clocked ARR AUM of over ₹700 crores over the last nine

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ROHIT S. BHASE
chunks.text:
months. The expected synergies from 360 ONE capital are now visible. Large IP mandates drew meaningful revenue accretion alongside an active block deal calendar. With strong ECM pipeline and expansion in research coverage, the franchise is gaining scale and building a more durable revenue base. Our collaboration with UBS continues to progress across bidirectional client reference, cross-platform product access, and exchange of best practices.
 In the asset management segment, ARR AUM stood at a little over ₹100,000 crores, up
9.4% year-on-year. Net flows improved to ₹1,492 crores after the large SMA redemptions in Q1. ARR revenue was ₹203 crores with retentions of 79 basis points, and operating PBT was ₹108 crores. In alternates, AIF AUM grew 27.9% year-on-year to ₹58,139 crores. We are amongst the leaders in private equity and credit space in India. During the quarter, we launched and mobilized funds across categories, including multi-stage AI fund, defence and space fund, ARISE credit fund. The pipeline remains strong for the coming quarters. In public markets, fund performance was strengthened, and our SIF strategy has gained traction with Dyna-SIF AUM crossing ₹1,000 crores. We won our first European institutional mandate and received a top-up from an existing global mandate.
 Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear in wealth, focus on adding new clients, raising

 Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear in wealth, focus on adding new clients, raising
RM productivity, and scaling reference across 360 ONE ecosystem. In asset management, we will keep sharpening our alternates offering, expand our institutional reach, diversify domestic distribution, and build out the SIF platform. And in 360 ONE capital, the priority is converting the ECM pipeline, strengthening the team, and expanding research coverage. All of this will be delivered with continued cost discipline and technology as a key lever.
 COMPASS, our proprietary and governed AI layer, is live across wealth, asset
management, and enterprise functions. It gives the RM a single integrated interface for research and product knowledge, market intelligence, prospecting, and pitch preparation. A 360-degree view of each client's family holdings, and portfolio, and service and business at risk alerts with next best actions. COMPASS runs entirely within 360 ONE environment with strict access controls. Client data never goes outside, and no data is used to train external models. The aim is simple, more time with clients, and a platform that scales efficiently. We do not judge COMPASS on usage, but on definite outcomes, which is efficiency, commercial impact, quality, and control.

− Thank you, Anil. A very good evening to all the participants. FY26 has been a landmark
year for 360 ONE, one in which we have delivered strong financial outcomes, and also meaningfully expanded the platform to complete our flywheel. Our core tenets - growth, resilience and agility have once again been validated in a year that tested markets and businesses alike. FY26 was characterized by complex interplay of global and domestic factors. Indian capital markets saw periods of increased volatility driven by evolving geopolitical dynamics and shifting global sentiments. While equity indices touched bullish levels in the first half, markets witnessed phases of correction and sectoral rotation through the year, testing investor conviction. Encouragingly, the Indian wealth and asset management ecosystem remained resilient, supported by record SIP contributions, sustained monetization activity across IPOs, block deals, private equity exits and a growing investor preference for professionally managed and alternate asset classes. A progressive regulatory environment continues to strengthen transparency, investor confidence and long-term capital formation.

But at an operating philosophy level, a very conservative and simple way to explain it is we typically start looking at carry only once the fund has met the hurdle for the entire life of the fund. That's really when the carry starts kicking in. So, it's a 5-year fund or a 6-year fund, it effectively has to beat the carry for the entire time period. And only then does the fund become carryable in any way. And once the fund becomes carryable, obviously, we take a slight bit of a discount in terms of market values and stuff like that and then start accounting for it. So, at the simplest level, it's not as if we are measuring the fund after one year, and it has to meet the hurdle after one year, and then we start accounting for carry. It has to meet the hurdle for the entire lifetime of the fund, and only then it comes into carry. So, I would say outside of large market variations, the carry which we are carrying is quite conservative and within range in terms of an overall fund list and broad maturity dates and so on. And maybe just a comment whether the fund is a carry fund or a fixed fee fund, maybe Sanjay can put it up on Excel.

360 ONE WAM Earnings’ Call - Q3 FY26 − Mr. Anil Mascarenhas - 360 ONE WAM:
− Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to 360 ONE WAM earnings call for Q3
FY26.
− As a reminder, all participant lines will be on listen-only mode. In case you wish to ask any
questions or require assistance during the conference, kindly signal the host by tapping on the raised hand icon.
− Please note, this conference is being recorded.
− On the call today, we have with us Mr. Karan Bhagat, MD and CEO, Mr. Yatin Shah, CEO
of the Wealth Business, Mr. Anshuman Maheshwary, Chief Operating Officer, and Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa, CFO.
− I now hand it over to Sanjay Wadhwa to take this conference ahead. Thank you.

− Thank you, Anil.
− Very good evening to all the participants. Over the past year, Indian capital markets

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · ROHIT SHRINIWAS BHASE
chunks.text:
− Very good evening to all the participants. Over the past year, Indian capital markets
navigated a period of heightened volatility shaped by evolving geopolitical dynamics and intermittent bouts of market consolidation. Encouragingly, even in such challenging market environment, the asset and wealth management ecosystem continued to demonstrate resilience with healthy inflows driven by record levels of mutual fund SIP contributions, sustained activity in terms of monetization events, and a growing investor preference for alternate asset classes.
− Coming to our business, our total ARR AUM increased to Rs 3,17,906 crores - up 28% year-
on-year with Wealth ARR AUM at Rs 218,957 crores and Asset Management ARR AUM at Rs 98,949 crores. This growth was supported by strong net flows at Rs. 14,758 crores in Q3 FY26 and Rs. 46,890 crores for 9m FY26. We expect this momentum to sustain as our newly onboarded high-quality teams continue to mature and achieve scale. In asset management, flows remain firmly on track supported by healthy demand across points spanning all asset classes. The asset management business saw good mobilizations during the quarter with over Rs 2,000 crores raised in our real asset strategy, Rs 2,500 crores of commitments in our private credit strategy, and Rs 2,000 crores raised in our mid and small cap focused listed strategy.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · ROHIT SHRINIWAS BHASE
chunks.text:
− Our ARR revenue in the quarter grew 45.4% YoY at Rs 619 crores led by strong asset
growth as well as improved retentions. Our ARR revenue as a percentage of total revenue
from operations stood at 77%. ARR retention remained strong at 81 basis points. Incremental carry revenue during the quarter contributed about approx. 6 basis points during the quarter, and the retentions are expected to normalize in the quarters to come. Transaction and broking revenues rose by 4.2% to Rs 186 crores. As stated in our previous quarter, revenue from institutional equities business of B&K, which is now being rebranded to 360 ONE Capital, is being classified as TBR. This business incubation meaningfully enhances the sustainability of TBR revenues and is expected to moderate the periodic volatility experienced in the past, thereby improving the overall quality of predictability of earnings.
− Total revenue increased by 21.8% to Rs 826 crores, driven by strong growth in both wealth

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · ROHIT SHRINIWAS BHASE
chunks.text:
− Total revenue increased by 21.8% to Rs 826 crores, driven by strong growth in both wealth
and asset verticals, partially offset by lower other income. Total costs were flat as compared to the previous quarter at Rs 399 crores, with the corresponding cost-to- income ratio at 48.3%. This is after factoring in the estimated impact of the new labour code, which in our case was not very material, at Rs 7.5 crores. We expect gradual improvement in this CI metric for the consolidated business over the coming quarters as we scale up and drive synergies from strategic initiatives, as well as the incoming teams in the Wealth UHNI segment.
− We are very happy to report that the company recorded its highest ever quarterly PAT at
Rs 331 crores, an increase of 20.3% year-on-year. Tangible ROE rose to 21% as against 20.4% in the previous quarter. This ratio is expected to improve in the coming quarters as additional capital deployed in our lending and alternate businesses in FY25 begins to reflect in the overall earnings.
− With that, I would like to hand over to Anshuman to cover key business and strategic
highlights.
− Mr. Anshuman Maheshwary - Chief Operating Officer, 360 ONE WAM:
− Thanks, Sanjay.
− Good evening, everyone.
− Building on Sanjay's thoughts on our overall business performance, I would like to begin
with some comments on our core businesses.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · ROHIT SHRINIWAS BHASE
chunks.text:
with some comments on our core businesses.

at over Rs 26,000 crores, having already equalled our full year 2025 numbers. Despite attrition-related outflows that we've spoken about earlier in H1, we've delivered strong organic net flows of Rs 19,000 crores or 12% of our opening ARR AUM in Wealth Management in this 9-month period. The strong performance reflects the fundamental strength of our franchise, the differentiated platform proposition and products, and most importantly, the continued ability to attract senior talent across our key geographies. The total net flows in Wealth stands at approximately Rs 40,000 crores, with the flows being spread across the different regions. Within Asset Management, we continue to witness
strong flows across asset classes. Net flows of over Rs 4,400 crores for this quarter were driven by new funds launched, as well as inflows in existing strategies in the listed, unlisted, credit and real estate space.
− While we maintain our leadership on advising global institutions on listed equities, we are

chunks.text:

chunks.text:
− A quick update on the key strategic initiatives. Starting with UBS, I am pleased to
announce that signing of our comprehensive Global Collaboration Framework for Wealth was completed in November of last year. We are already witnessing encouraging early traction on cross-border client referrals and remain excited about emerging synergies in asset management as well as other areas. With strong leadership commitment from both organizations, we are well positioned to unlock the potential of this partnership and will continue to update on the progress over the next few quarters.

continues to strengthen as we gain momentum in client additions as well as flows. With over 60 RMs across 12 locations, we are now well poised to accelerate the scaling up and build this segment as a vital feeder pipeline as well for our UHNI proposition.
− Thirdly, ET Money is undergoing a transition from a transaction-led investing app to a
comprehensive wealth platform for the affluent segment, with monetization embedded at every stage. By combining choice-led engagement models and expanding product suite, which aligns with our core proposition and technology-enabled human advice, ET Money is continuing to build a differentiated yet scalable moat which we are quite excited by.

chunks.text:
− And lastly, we are pleased to share that B&K Securities is now rebranded as 360 ONE
Capital, integrating corporate and institutional equities as core capabilities. This integration not only expands our capital markets footprint but reinforces our positioning as one of India's most comprehensive financial services platforms, spanning wealth management, asset management, alternates, lending, enhanced institutional and capital market capabilities, as well as superior global access.
− Overall, we remain focused on consolidating our multiple business lines to deliver a full-
stack financial services offering aimed at further strengthening our leadership position with our core clients.

operations, cyber security, and client-facing innovation. We are advancing AI-powered pilots across key functions to drive efficiency gains and informed decision making, positioning ourselves to expand these capabilities as they further mature.
− Lastly, I would like to thank our clients and stakeholders for their continued trust and
confidence, which has been integral to our journey and progress. And with that, I'd like to hand it over to Karan for his thoughts.

− So, as we look forward and look at the back, we continue to be super positive on the

chunks.text:
− So, as we look forward and look at the back, we continue to be super positive on the

One is the UHNI Wealth Management business, and second is the Alternates business over the last eight to nine years. We continue to remain extremely buoyant about those two businesses. Our brand recall as well as our acceptability among clients above Rs 50 crores, continues to remain at the highest. Our proposition has become deeper and deeper. Both monetization on the listed side and unlisted side, sometimes even change of wealth manager on the ground without liquidity events, all of them continue to be fairly active programs for us. continue to remain very buoyant about the Alternates space and with the new regulations, both on the LVF side, as well as the co-investment vehicle side, it gives us a lot of additional ammunition to be able to really take advantage of the Rs 50,000 crores we've already kind of built in the space over the last 7 to 8 years. And most of our old clients continue to come into the new schemes as the older schemes continue to mature.

chunks.text:
